meta.title: Interrogation: The Room With No File
meta.notes: Five-minute interrogation prototype. Fixed four-choice interface. S09 presents final decision labels (continued detention, authorize release, escalate case, walk away/say nothing). Endings S10-S13 include a single restart choice (PLAY AGAIN) back to S01; remaining buttons are blank labels but still route to S01 to avoid dead UI. Printed CHOICES blocks preserved for readability. ASCII-only. Replay one-liners included in S01, S02, S03, S04, S06 via [REPLAY] marker.
meta.blurb: You enter an interrogation room with no file, no transcript, and no certainty. The only thing you know is that this meeting matters.

S01.text:
The room smells faintly of disinfectant.

The person across from you sits with their hands folded. Not restrained. Not relaxed.

They look up when you enter.

"Am I free to go?"

[REPLAY]
The question lands faster this time, like it has been asked before.

CHOICES

APPLY PRESSURE
You establish authority immediately. You are not here to comfort them.

OFFER UNDERSTANDING
You lower the temperature. You signal that you are listening.

CHALLENGE STATEMENT
You reject the framing and force clarity.

SAY NOTHING
You let silence begin the interrogation.

S02.text:
You take your seat. The chair legs scrape lightly on tile.

They keep their hands folded. Their posture is measured.

"I have already told them everything I know," they say.

They do not sound angry.
They sound practiced.

[REPLAY]
You remember this line. The delivery is identical.

CHOICES

APPLY PRESSURE
You tighten the room and test the script.

OFFER UNDERSTANDING
You invite deviation without threat.

CHALLENGE STATEMENT
You demand specifics.

SAY NOTHING
You let discomfort grow.

S03.text:
"You people always think you know how this goes," they say.

They stop themselves.

"...sorry."

[REPLAY]
Last time, you believed that apology meant something.

CHOICES

APPLY PRESSURE
You push past the apology.

OFFER UNDERSTANDING
You treat the slip as a crack.

CHALLENGE STATEMENT
You isolate the phrase and force ownership.

SAY NOTHING
You let the apology hang.

S04.text:
"I did not say I was there," they say.

You are fairly certain they did.

There is no transcript. No file. Just memory.

[REPLAY]
You hesitate, not because you doubt them, but because you doubt yourself.

CHOICES

APPLY PRESSURE
You assert your certainty.

OFFER UNDERSTANDING
You allow room for error.

CHALLENGE STATEMENT
You demand a concrete anchor.

SAY NOTHING
You let the contradiction sit.

S05.text:
Their jaw tightens.

"You do not understand what happens if I talk," they say.

It is not a confession.
It is a warning.
Or fear.
Or a test.

CHOICES

APPLY PRESSURE
You treat fear as leverage.

OFFER UNDERSTANDING
You invite explanation without promise.

CHALLENGE STATEMENT
You demand they define the threat.

SAY NOTHING
You offer only space.

S06.text:
The clock on the wall clicks louder than it should.

A long silence settles between you.

They glance at your hands, then your face, like they are trying to measure you.

[REPLAY]
You know how long this silence can last. It still feels longer.

CHOICES

APPLY PRESSURE
You break the silence hard.

OFFER UNDERSTANDING
You break it gently.

CHALLENGE STATEMENT
You force a response.

SAY NOTHING
You let silence work.

S07.text:
"I just want this to be over," they say.

Their eyes flick toward the door.

That movement could mean escape.
Or rescue.
Or threat.

CHOICES

APPLY PRESSURE
You do not let them escape the moment.

OFFER UNDERSTANDING
You humanize the plea.

CHALLENGE STATEMENT
You reject comfort for clarity.

SAY NOTHING
You wait.

S08.text:
"If I leave here..." they start.

They stop.

"...that is on you, right?"

They are offering you weight.
They are handing you responsibility.

You still do not know what the stakes are.
Only that the meeting matters.

CHOICES

APPLY PRESSURE
You refuse the moral trap.

OFFER UNDERSTANDING
You accept the weight.

CHALLENGE STATEMENT
You confront the manipulation.

SAY NOTHING
You do not answer.

S09.text:
The room waits.

This is the decision.

CHOICES

REQUEST CONTINUED DETENTION
You choose to hold them. You treat uncertainty as danger.

AUTHORIZE RELEASE
You choose to release them. You refuse to cage someone on instinct.

ESCALATE THE CASE
You pass the weight upward and invite a bigger machine into the room.

WALK AWAY
You do nothing now and let time choose for you.

S10.text:
You request continued detention.

Paperwork replaces eye contact.

They do not plead.
They do not rage.
They only watch you like they are memorizing your face.

You never learn if it was justice or caution.

Only that you chose control over doubt.

CHOICES

PLAY AGAIN
Return to the beginning.

S11.text:
You authorize their release.

They stand slowly. No gratitude. No relief.

At the door, they pause like they might say something.

They do not.

You never learn if mercy was earned.

Only that you chose humanity over certainty.

CHOICES

PLAY AGAIN
Return to the beginning.

S12.text:
You escalate the case.

The room changes as soon as you do. More eyes. More distance.

They stop speaking to you and start speaking past you.

You are no longer in the room when it concludes.

Only that you handed the weight upward.

CHOICES

PLAY AGAIN
Return to the beginning.

S13.text:
You walk away without deciding.

Time chooses for you.

In the hall, you tell yourself you needed more certainty.

Later, you realize certainty was never on the table.

You replay the silence longer than anything that was said.

CHOICES

PLAY AGAIN
Return to the beginning.
